history.dynasty: Silhara dynasty (original); rebuilt under private Gaud Saraswat patronage
history.period: Original construction 1127 AD; destroyed 16th century (Portuguese); rebuilt 1715 AD
history.summary: The Walkeshwar Temple, also called the Baan Ganga Temple, is an ancient Shiva temple at Walkeshwar on Malabar Hill in South Mumbai, beside the freshwater Banganga Tank. Legend holds that Rama paused here on his way to Lanka, made a Shiva linga of sand (Valuka Iswar, the origin of the name Walkeshwar), and shot an arrow (bana) to bring the Ganga to this spot, creating the Banganga. The temple and tank were built in 1127 AD by Lakshman Prabhu, a Gaud Saraswat Brahmin minister in the court of the Silhara kings. The temple was destroyed during Portuguese rule in the 16th century and rebuilt in 1715 by the Mumbai businessman and philanthropist Rama Kamath (Kamati). The main temple has been substantially reconstructed in modern times (reinforced concrete), and by 1860 some 10-20 smaller temples and 50 dharamshalas had come up around the tank. The temple and much of the surrounding property belong to the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin Temple Trust, with Shri Kashi Math and Shri Kavle (Kaivalya) Math branches on the tank's banks.

town_description: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial capital, a coastal metropolis built on seven islands reclaimed over centuries. Malabar Hill, at the city's highest point in South Mumbai, is its most prestigious residential quarter, home to the Walkeshwar Temple, the Banganga Tank, the Governor's residence, and the Hanging Gardens, with sweeping views of the Arabian Sea and Back Bay.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai; approx. 28-30 km by road via the Bandra-Worli Sea Link (verify).
travel.railway: Churchgate (Western Railway) approx. 3-4 km; Grant Road station approx. 2-3 km (verify). Local taxis and BEST buses serve Malabar Hill.
travel.road: Walkeshwar is on Malabar Hill in South Mumbai, reachable by road via Walkeshwar Road / Banganga Cross Lane; city buses, taxis and auto-rickshaws available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Mahashivratri and the Banganga Festival (music festival season, typically January) are the grandest times but draw crowds.
